name: side_to_move_defined
assertion: state.turn is either white or black.
why: Active color is part of the state and repetition identity.

name: color_occupancies_disjoint
assertion: white_occupancy & black_occupancy == 0.
why: No square can hold both colors.

name: occupancy_union_matches_total
assertion: all_occupancy == (white_occupancy | black_occupancy).
why: Internal occupancy masks must agree.

name: piece_type_bitboards_disjoint
assertion: No square appears in more than one piece-type set.
why: A square cannot simultaneously contain multiple piece types.

name: board_array_matches_bitboards
assertion: Mailbox/array view and bitboards encode the same board.
why: Mixed representations drift easily after make/unmake bugs.

name: piece_lists_match_board
assertion: Piece lists and piece-count tables match square contents exactly.
why: Piece-list corruption is a classic move/unmove failure mode.

name: square_uniqueness
assertion: Each occupied square contains exactly one piece record.
why: Duplicate square ownership indicates structural corruption.

name: exactly_one_white_king
assertion: There is exactly one white king on the board.
why: Standard chess requires one king per side.

name: exactly_one_black_king
assertion: There is exactly one black king on the board.
why: Standard chess requires one king per side.

name: white_piece_budget
assertion: White has at most 16 men.
why: A side cannot retain more than its original sixteen men.

name: black_piece_budget
assertion: Black has at most 16 men.
why: A side cannot retain more than its original sixteen men.

name: white_pawn_budget
assertion: White has at most 8 pawns.
why: A side starts with eight pawns and promotions remove pawns.

name: black_pawn_budget
assertion: Black has at most 8 pawns.
why: A side starts with eight pawns and promotions remove pawns.

name: total_piece_budget
assertion: Total occupied squares with pieces is at most 32.
why: Orthodox chess has 32 physical men maximum.

name: no_pawns_on_backrank
assertion: No pawn occupies rank 1 or rank 8.
why: A pawn that reaches the back rank must promote immediately.

name: castling_rights_mask_sane
assertion: Castling-right bits are from the supported set only.
why: Corrupted rights create false legal moves and false repetition keys.

name: castling_rights_structurally_consistent
assertion: If castling rights are present, the corresponding king and rook mapping is structurally valid for the chosen variant.
why: Libraries and engines validate castling rights against board structure.
implementation_notes: In orthodox chess this usually means king on e1/e8 and rook on a/h; in Chess960 use your start-file mapping.

name: ep_square_shape_spec
assertion: Under FEN-spec mode, EP square is absent or on rank 3/6 consistent with the external notation rules.
why: The FEN spec defines EP as a target square field of the state.
implementation_notes: This is the external I/O policy, not necessarily the internal canonical form.

name: ep_square_shape_strict
assertion: Under strict-internal mode, EP square is absent or also satisfies local capture preconditions.
why: Stockfish sanitizes EP more aggressively than the original FEN spec.
implementation_notes: Recommended internal canonicalization policy if you want a tighter state invariant.

name: halfmove_clock_nonnegative
assertion: halfmove_clock >= 0.
why: The halfmove clock is a nonnegative FEN field.

name: fullmove_number_positive
assertion: fullmove_number >= 1.
why: The fullmove number in FEN starts at 1 and increments after Black's move.

name: ply_counter_consistent
assertion: If a separate ply counter is stored, it is consistent with fullmove_number and side_to_move.
why: Counter drift breaks PGN/FEN export and search bookkeeping.

name: zobrist_hash_matches_recompute
assertion: Position hash equals a clean recomputation from board + turn + castling + EP.
why: TT corruption and repetition bugs often surface here first.

name: pawn_hash_matches_recompute
assertion: Pawn hash equals a clean recomputation from pawn locations and any side-dependent pawn features if used.
why: Useful for engines with pawn hash tables.

name: material_key_matches_recompute
assertion: Material key / material signature matches recomputation.
why: Stockfish checks material consistency in pos_is_ok().

name: attack_cache_matches_recompute
assertion: Cached attack maps match recomputation from the board.
why: Invalid attack caches create false checks and false legal moves.

name: checkers_cache_matches_recompute
assertion: Cached checker set equals recomputation.
why: Many engines cache 'checkers' or 'in_check' incrementally.

name: pinners_blockers_cache_matches_recompute
assertion: Pinned-piece and blocker caches match a fresh computation.
why: Pinned move legality is highly sensitive to stale caches.

name: eval_cache_matches_recompute
assertion: If incremental material/PSQT/eval caches exist, they match full recomputation in debug mode.
why: This catches silent evaluation drift unrelated to rule legality.

name: nnue_accumulator_matches_refresh
assertion: If NNUE or similar accumulators are incremental, a forced refresh matches the current accumulator.
why: Search correctness depends on cache coherence even when move legality is correct.
implementation_notes: Optional if the engine uses incremental neural accumulators.

name: move_stack_frame_integrity
assertion: Top undo frame is structurally complete whenever a move is pushed.
why: Unmake correctness requires exact saved state.

name: repetition_stack_length_consistent
assertion: The repetition-history stack length matches the move stack / ply count policy.
why: Repetition logic depends on a faithful key history.

name: side_not_to_move_not_in_check
assertion: In a legal resulting position, the side that just moved is not left in check.
why: FIDE legality forbids making a move that leaves your own king in check.

name: kings_not_adjacent
assertion: The two kings do not attack each other from adjacent squares.
why: Adjacent kings imply an illegal position.

name: checker_count_at_most_two
assertion: The checked side has at most two independent checking pieces.
why: In orthodox chess, more than two simultaneous checkers is impossible.

name: opposite_check_rejected
assertion: Reject states where the side not to move is in check.
why: python-chess exposes this as OPPOSITE_CHECK and Stockfish rejects king-capturable states.

name: impossible_check_patterns_rejected
assertion: Reject or warn on impossible check geometries that cannot arise from a legal last move.
why: python-chess includes IMPOSSIBLE_CHECK and TOO_MANY_CHECKERS as import-time sanity checks.

name: legal_moves_are_pseudolegal
assertion: Every move in the legal move list is also pseudo-legal under piece movement rules.
why: A legal move generator should refine, not contradict, pseudo-legal generation.

name: legal_filter_removes_self_check_only
assertion: Pseudo-legal moves become legal exactly when they do not leave the mover's king in check.
why: The difference between pseudo-legal and legal move sets should be explained by king safety.

name: no_move_captures_king
assertion: No legal move captures a king.
why: Checkmate ends the game; kings are never captured in legal chess.

name: king_move_destination_not_attacked
assertion: Every legal king move lands on a square not attacked by the opponent.
why: This is the core king-safety condition.

name: pinned_piece_moves_preserve_ray
assertion: A legal move by a pinned piece stays on the pin ray unless it captures the pinning piece in a legal way.
why: Pinned-piece handling is a common movegen bug source.

name: castling_requires_right
assertion: A castling move is legal only if the relevant historical castling right is still present.
why: Castling legality depends partly on history, not just geometry.

name: castling_path_empty
assertion: All squares between king and rook are empty for a legal castling move.
why: FIDE requires no intervening pieces.

name: castling_squares_not_attacked
assertion: For a legal castling move, the king's start, transit, and destination squares are not under attack.
why: FIDE castling rules explicitly require this.

name: castling_rook_king_destinations_correct
assertion: A castling move relocates king and rook to the correct final squares under the supported variant.
why: Move application must match the rules exactly.

name: castling_forbidden_while_in_check
assertion: Castling is not legal when the king starts the move in check.
why: FIDE explicitly forbids castling out of check.

name: en_passant_requires_last_move_history
assertion: An en passant capture is legal only on the reply immediately following the opponent's double pawn push.
why: This is a history-sensitive rule, not a geometric rule alone.

name: en_passant_target_square_correct
assertion: A pseudo-legal en passant capture targets the current EP square and the captured pawn sits on the passed square.
why: EP application bugs often remove the wrong pawn or square.

name: en_passant_preserves_king_safety
assertion: An en passant move is legal only if removing both pawns does not expose the moving side's king.
why: EP is the special move most likely to break incremental attack logic.

name: promotion_from_last_rank_transition_only
assertion: A promotion occurs only when a pawn moves from its penultimate rank to the back rank.
why: Promotion cannot happen from arbitrary squares.

name: promotion_piece_set_restricted
assertion: Promotion result is one of queen, rook, bishop, or knight.
why: FIDE restricts promotion choices to these four pieces.

name: promotion_replaces_pawn_immediately
assertion: After promotion, the pawn no longer exists on the destination square; the promoted piece does.
why: Promotion is immediate and final on that move.

name: double_pawn_push_preconditions
assertion: A two-square pawn advance starts from the home rank, crosses an empty square, and lands on an empty square.
why: Piece movement rules define this precisely.

name: pawn_move_geometry_correct
assertion: Single pushes, captures, and promotions follow pawn geometry exactly for the side to move.
why: Pawn bugs generate many downstream legality failures.

name: slider_paths_unobstructed
assertion: Bishop, rook, and queen moves traverse unobstructed rays.
why: Ray bugs create phantom moves and missed attacks.

name: knight_move_geometry_correct
assertion: Knight moves use L-shaped geometry and ignore interposing pieces.
why: Knights are the main non-ray exception.

name: king_move_geometry_correct
assertion: Non-castling king moves are one square in any direction and obey occupancy/attack rules.
why: Separates basic geometry from castling logic.

name: checkmate_definition_exact
assertion: If in check and with no legal moves, the state is checkmate.
why: Terminal classification should match the Laws of Chess exactly.

name: stalemate_definition_exact
assertion: If not in check and with no legal moves, the state is stalemate.
why: Terminal classification should match the Laws of Chess exactly.

name: dead_position_not_conflated_with_simple_material
assertion: Do not equate 'dead position' with a simplistic insufficient-material heuristic; if using a heuristic, label it as such.
why: FIDE's dead-position rule is semantic, not merely a material-count table.
implementation_notes: Use exact dead-position logic if you implement it; otherwise expose a weaker 'insufficient material heuristic' name.

name: legal_move_count_matches_recompute
assertion: A fresh legal move recomputation yields the same count and set as the incremental generator.
why: This is a strong deep-check invariant.

name: attackers_to_consistent
assertion: attackers_to(square, side) matches a fresh attack generator or inverse move generator.
why: Attack queries are used across check, SEE, pins, castling, and evaluation.

name: attacked_squares_stable_after_make_unmake
assertion: Attack maps before a move equal attack maps after make+unmake.
why: This catches incremental attack-cache drift.

name: castling_rights_monotone
assertion: Castling rights never reappear once lost.
why: Castling rights are historical entitlements, not dynamic geometric facts.

name: king_move_clears_both_rights
assertion: Moving a king clears both castling rights for that side.
why: This follows directly from the castling rule.

name: rook_home_move_clears_right
assertion: Moving a rook from its original castling square clears the corresponding castling right.
why: The relevant rook must not have moved previously.

name: rook_home_capture_clears_right
assertion: Capturing a rook on its original castling square clears that side's corresponding castling right if still present.
why: Rights can be lost by rook disappearance as well as rook movement.

name: castling_move_clears_side_rights
assertion: Executing castling clears both castling rights for the moving side.
why: After the king moves, castling is permanently lost.

name: ep_square_set_per_policy
assertion: After a legal double pawn push, set the EP square according to the chosen policy (spec-FEN or strict-captureable).
why: The specification and internal canonicalization policy may differ here.
implementation_notes: Preserve external I/O fidelity even if your internal canonical state is stricter.

name: ep_square_cleared_when_expired
assertion: EP availability disappears after one opponent reply if unused.
why: FIDE says en passant is legal only on the immediately following move.

name: ep_square_cleared_on_non_qualifying_move
assertion: Any move that is not a fresh double pawn push leaves no EP target square afterward.
why: A stale EP square creates false legal moves and wrong repetition keys.

name: halfmove_reset_on_pawn_move
assertion: Any pawn move resets the halfmove clock to zero.
why: This is defined by FEN and the move-counting rules.

name: halfmove_reset_on_capture
assertion: Any capture resets the halfmove clock to zero.
why: This is defined by FEN and the move-counting rules.

name: halfmove_increment_otherwise
assertion: A non-pawn, non-capture move increments the halfmove clock by one.
why: Halfmove maintenance drives 50/75-move logic.

name: fullmove_increment_after_black
assertion: fullmove_number increments after Black's move only.
why: This is the FEN fullmove-number convention.

name: undo_frame_is_lossless
assertion: Undo metadata stores enough information to restore board, turn, rights, EP, clocks, and hashes exactly.
why: Exact unmake is the linchpin of search correctness.

name: make_unmake_roundtrip_exact
assertion: Applying a move and then unmaking it restores the pre-move state exactly, including hashes and counters.
why: This is the most valuable transition invariant in engines.

name: rebuild_from_history_matches_state
assertion: Replaying move history from the root yields the exact current state.
why: This protects against long-range drift in incremental logic.

name: null_move_toggles_turn_and_clears_ep
assertion: If null move pruning is supported, null move flips side to move, clears EP, and updates clocks without mutating pieces or rights.
why: Null move is engine-internal but still needs invariant coverage.
implementation_notes: Only relevant if the engine implements null moves.

name: repetition_key_includes_relevant_state
assertion: Position identity for repetition includes piece placement, side to move, castling rights, and relevant EP availability.
why: FIDE treats positions as different if possible moves differ because of castling or EP.

name: repetition_history_consistent
assertion: The repetition table / key multiset matches the actual stack of visited positions.
why: Threefold/fivefold draw logic depends on exact history accounting.

name: threefold_and_fivefold_derived_from_history
assertion: Threefold-claim and fivefold-automatic draw states derive from actual repeated position keys, not from ad hoc heuristics.
why: These are history-sensitive, not purely local board properties.

name: fifty_and_seventyfive_move_rules_from_clock
assertion: 50-move claimability and 75-move automatic draw logic derive from the halfmove clock and applicable exceptions.
why: These rules are defined at the game-state level.

name: fen_roundtrip_exact_under_io_policy
assertion: serialize_fen(parse_fen(fen)) preserves the intended external FEN policy or normalizes only as documented.
why: Roundtrip correctness matters for external interfaces and debugging.

name: pgn_san_roundtrip_when_supported
assertion: If SAN/PGN is implemented, parsing emitted SAN from the same state reproduces the original move.
why: Notation code is another high-value surface for rule bugs.

name: root_state_preserved_across_search
assertion: Search must not mutate the root position after completion, including clocks, stack, and hash.
why: Search bugs can leak mutations via TT, PV, or null-move paths.

name: principal_variation_replay_legal
assertion: Moves reported in the PV are legal when replayed from the root under the engine's own rules.
why: This validates search output against the rule layer.

name: tt_move_legal_in_position
assertion: A transposition-table move retrieved for a position is legal or at least pseudo-legal under the current state policy.
why: Illegal TT moves indicate key collisions or state corruption.

name: promotion_budget_feasible_per_side
assertion: The number of extra queens/rooks/bishops/knights on a side is explainable by missing pawns via promotion.
why: Material configurations can be locally plausible but globally unreachable.

name: global_promotion_budget_feasible
assertion: Combined extra material across both sides does not exceed the total number of promotable pawns that must have disappeared.
why: This is a stronger global promotion sanity check.

name: pawn_capture_budget_feasible
assertion: Pawn-file displacement and survivor counts do not require more captures than are available.
why: Retrograde reasoning often starts with pawn capture budgets.

name: pawn_origin_feasible
assertion: Each pawn arrangement is plausibly derivable from home files under capture constraints; obviously impossible origins are flagged.
why: Many unreachable positions hide in pawn structure, not in piece movement.

name: bishop_color_complex_feasible
assertion: Bishop counts and square-color occupancy are plausible under promotion accounting.
why: Bishop color-complex arguments are a standard retrograde tool.

name: rook_knight_queen_excess_explained
assertion: Surplus rooks, knights, or queens imply corresponding promoted pawns and capture history budgets.
why: This turns raw material counts into a stronger reachability filter.

name: impossible_checker_geometry_warned
assertion: Imported positions with checker constellations that cannot arise from any legal last move are rejected or warned.
why: python-chess exposes impossible-check style statuses for this reason.

name: imported_position_validity_level_explicit
assertion: Imported FENs are classified as basic-valid, heuristic-reachability-pass/fail, or trusted-generated; do not collapse these categories.
why: The research literature distinguishes local validity from true reachability.

name: reachable_by_construction_flag
assertion: States produced from the initial position by your own legal move engine are tagged as trusted-by-construction.
why: This is the cleanest way to avoid re-solving reachability on internal states.

name: proof_game_hook_optional
assertion: Provide a hook for an optional proof-game / retrograde module if arbitrary external legal-position guarantees are required.
why: Reachability is substantially harder than local validation.

name: clone_equality
assertion: Cloning a state yields an equivalent state in all semantically relevant fields.
why: Basic object-copy correctness supports every other test harness.

name: fen_roundtrip_normalized_equality
assertion: parse(serialize(state)) == normalize(state) under the declared EP/castling I/O policy.
why: Serialization roundtrips are a cheap metamorphic test.

name: vertical_mirror_color_swap_perft
assertion: After vertical board mirror plus color swap (and corresponding turn/castling/EP remap), perft at depth d is unchanged.
why: The rule layer should be symmetric under color-swapping mirror transforms when state metadata is transformed consistently.

name: horizontal_reflection_perft
assertion: After horizontal reflection (a-file <-> h-file) with castling/EP file remapping, perft at depth d is unchanged.
why: Orthodox chess rules are file-symmetric when state metadata is transformed consistently.

name: make_unmake_involution
assertion: state == unmake(make(state, move)) for every legal move.
why: This is the canonical state-transition metamorphic relation for engines.

name: move_order_independence_of_rule_layer
assertion: Sorted legal move sets are invariant under any internal move ordering changes.
why: Search may depend on order, but rule correctness must not.
implementation_notes: Apply to the rule layer. Do not assume evaluation or search scores are identical at all depths.

name: search_does_not_mutate_state
assertion: A pure search call leaves the input state unchanged.
why: This is a higher-level metamorphic invariant around search entry/exit.

name: color_swap_eval_sign
assertion: For an evaluation function expressed from one fixed perspective, color-swapping a position should flip the sign under a documented convention.
why: Useful for evaluation sanity checks, but not a strict rule oracle.
implementation_notes: Use only for evaluation testing, not for move legality.

name: tablebase_wdl_matches_oracle
assertion: On Syzygy-eligible positions, WDL/DTZ results match the exact tablebase oracle.
why: Tablebases are the strongest exact oracles available for many endings.

name: reference_engine_legal_moves_match
assertion: On random reachable positions, legal move sets match a trusted reference implementation such as python-chess or a reference engine wrapper.
why: Differential testing is one of the highest-value complements to invariants.

name: reference_engine_terminal_flags_match
assertion: On random reachable positions, in-check/checkmate/stalemate/EP/castling availability agree with the reference implementation under the same policy.
why: Terminal-state and history bugs are common and easy to catch this way.

name: perft_reference_counts_match
assertion: Perft counts match the standard corpus on the included reference positions and depths.
why: Perft is the classic debugging oracle for move generation and make/unmake.
